study_identification_part.si4_title: Rightward brain structural asymmetry in young children with autism

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the study aims: to use developmental normative models to characterize atypical GMV asymmetry in ASD with/without DD/ID and DD/ID-only, and to relate deviations to behavioral/clinical measures and gene expression. This directly satisfies both criteria: explicit research objectives and purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Here, using the cross-sectional sMRI data of 1030 children under 8 years old, we employed developmental normative models to investigate the atypical development of gray matter volume (GMV) asymmetry ... and their associations with behavioral and clinical measures and transcription profiles.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: NEW normative model built using TD children (n=219 overall; 247 TD used for training cited later). QC standards are described (manual inspection to exclude motion artifacts; second QC; smoothing). However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria defining the TD reference cohort are not detailed beyond being age-matched typically developing children, and reasons/counts for exclusion are not fully enumerated.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: After imaging quality control (see below for details), the data of 1030 young children were employed for analysis, including ... 219 age-matched TD children ... Raw structural images were independently manually inspected ... to exclude those with obvious motion artefacts. ... we conducted the second round of quality control ...

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly modeled as covariates in the GPR normative models. Multi-site effects are addressed with ComBat harmonization, satisfying handling of site effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: GPR models of GMV asymmetry for each ROI were trained based on 247 TDs with age and sex as covariates. ... The ComBat analysis based on an empirical Bayes approach was utilized to harmonize the site effects.

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Primary data collection from two scanners/sites is described, including site identities, scanner models, and dataset source (Shanghai Autism Early Development Cohort).
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Participants were recruited from ... Shanghai Autism Early Development Cohort. ... The MRI data of 283 children ... collected at site 1 with a Philips Ingenia ... 747 children ... at site 2 with a Siemens Verio MRI scanner.

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Imaging modality (structural MRI, T1-weighted) and acquisition parameters (TR, TE, flip angle, FOV, voxel size, slice thickness/number) and equipment (Philips Ingenia; Siemens Verio) are fully specified.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Similar T1-weighted axial protocols ... For the Siemens Verio scanner: TR = 2300 ms, TE = 2.28 ms, flip angle = 8°, FOV = 192 mm * 192 mm; voxel size = 1*1*1 mm3; slice thickness = 1 mm, and slice number = 170. For the Philip Ingenia scanner: TR = 7.9 ms, TE = 3.5 ms, flip angle = 8°, FOV = 250 mm * 199 mm; voxel size = 1*1*1 mm3; slice thickness = 1 mm, and slice number = 170.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing software and steps are described: CAT12 for skull stripping/realignment, CHN-PD atlas registration/segmentation, QC procedures (manual + algorithmic), and SPM12 smoothing with 8 mm kernel.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: Raw structural images were ... inspected ... to exclude motion artefacts. After quality control, the preprocessing steps included skull stripping, and realignment using CAT12 and then reregistered and segmented based on the Chinese pediatric atlases (CHN-PD) ... second round of quality control ... Finally, smoothing using SPM12 with an 8 mm isotropic Gaussian kernel was conducted.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Fivefold cross-validation was conducted when training GPR models to avoid overfitting and select parameters; supplementary analysis reports high correlations between original and CV-based deviations, supporting internal validation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: Fivefold cross-validation was conducted to avoid overfitting and obtain optimal parameters. ... All correlations were higher than 0.948 and statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (corrected p < 0.05).

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study does not report applying the TD-trained normative model to an independent external healthy dataset beyond the two in-study acquisition sites.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No external healthy-control dataset application is described; modeling and validations are conducted within the recruited cohort across two sites.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is specified: Gaussian Process Regression implemented via the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit (PCNtoolkit), per-ROI models with covariates, and CV to tune parameters.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: ... using the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit with the Gaussian process regression (GPR) method ... GPR models ... were trained ... with age and sex as covariates. Fivefold cross-validation was conducted ...

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: The correlations between original GMV-lateralization deviations and 5-fold cross validation GMV-lateralization deviations ... All correlations were higher than 0.948 and statistically significant after Bonferroni correction.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation scores are defined as Z-scores relative to TD distributions, and the direction of group-level deviations is explained via one-sample t-tests (positive=more leftward, negative=more rightward). A quantitative threshold is provided for kurtosis (>5) but no explicit Z-thresholds for categorizing individuals (e.g., |Z|>1.96).
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: ... obtained the individual Z scores, which indicated the statistical estimate of the degree of deviation from TD distributions ... Notably, a positive t value indicated ... more leftward ... while a negative t value indicated increasing rightward asymmetry. ... kurtosis ... values above 5 were set as the threshold for abnormal criteria.
